reason: Despite the title, it is a review: compares REPORTED performance of 82 methods across benchmarks, no new experiments, so S not M
It argues a framing, then presents the authors' own system and evaluates it on two public benchmarks in a dedicated evaluation section. That matches rule 3 exactly. N, not P.

The paper does both jobs at scale: about 15 pages of unified review of existing methods and about 13 pages of new benchmark results. That clears the threshold easily. It is not a plain benchmark (N) because the review of existing methods is a stated co-contribution. Threshold used on all rows: new experiments count as 'substantial' only if they are a stated main contribution, get their own results section, are run by the authors over several tasks or datasets and produce new comparative findings

This is a vision or concept paper for an architecture class: use cases, design considerations, deployment models, challenges and comparison tables. There is no implementation or evaluation of its own, so it is not an N system paper. It is not mainly a literature synthesis either, since related work and prior-work numbers only support the concept. Rule 7 gives P. Borderline; S would also count as positive under rule 8.

The main job is a survey and taxonomy, but the authors also ran a new multi-task benchmark: a dedicated section of about 29% of the body, with new results. These are not numbers copied from the original papers. Under the threshold this is substantial, so M rather than S. This is the same standard that makes Core 13 M.

The full text resolves the uncertainty, so U is wrong. The largest part is a review of existing detection work. The proposed architecture is conceptual, has no results and is presented as 'a technical guide'. That makes it a challenges-and-opportunities review with a roadmap. S (P would also be acceptable under rule 8). Not N or M, because there are no new experiments.

The main contribution is a design space (taxonomy) synthesised from a structured review of existing kits and research, about two-thirds of the body. The authors' kits are short illustrative examples with no formal evaluation, so they are not a 'new system with evaluation' (M), and the review is not mere motivation (rule 2). S by main job. Borderline, because HCI design-space papers are often treated as N, but under this codebook a taxonomy built from the literature is S.
